plan.outcome7: By day 7 you'll be able to build and switch on one n8n workflow for a real task at your job, for example a new form response gets added to a spreadsheet and posts a Slack message, and when a run fails you can find the step that broke and fix it.
plan.horizon14: Later: two or three workflows running every day, each replacing one repetitive task you used to do by hand.
plan.horizon28: Later: a workflow with an AI step that drafts or sorts text, with a check in place so a bad result never reaches a colleague.

picture.name: A small assembly line
picture.line: Every workflow is a small assembly line: one bell starts it, each station does exactly one job, and the item moves down the belt from station to station until it is finished.

chapters.title: The bell that starts the line
chapters.covers: Every workflow begins with a trigger, the one event that wakes it up: a time of day, a form being submitted, or an app sending a signal. You set up n8n, build a workflow with a Schedule Trigger, and run it by hand.
chapters.outcome: You can build a workflow that wakes up on a schedule and does one visible thing, like sending yourself a message.
chapters.hook: Every automation you have ever used is three parts. You will build all three in 10 minutes.

chapters.title: Stations and the belt
chapters.covers: Each box in n8n is a node, a station that does one job. Data travels between them as items, small packets of named fields. You chain three nodes and read the output panel to see what each one passes on.
chapters.outcome: You can connect three nodes in a row and read exactly what each station hands to the next.
chapters.hook: A workflow that never starts does nothing. Which of 4 starters does your task need?

chapters.title: Plugging in your work apps
chapters.covers: To use Gmail, Google Sheets, Slack or similar, n8n needs credentials, a saved permission to act as you. You connect one app you use at work and read from it or write to it.
chapters.outcome: You can connect one work app to n8n and make it add a row or send a message.
chapters.hook: The box labelled 'name' and the box labelled 'Name' are different. This chapter stops that bug.

chapters.title: Passing parts between stations
chapters.covers: An expression, written between double curly braces, pulls a field from an earlier node into a later one. You use the Edit Fields node to rename and tidy data before it reaches an app.
chapters.outcome: You can take a name from step 1 and put it into a message sent in step 3.
chapters.hook: n8n has over 400 ready-made connections. Yours take about 4 minutes each to set up.

chapters.title: Sorting items down two belts
chapters.covers: The IF node checks a value and sends items down a true path or a false path. The Filter node drops items you do not want. You build a workflow that treats urgent and normal items differently.
chapters.outcome: You can route items down two different paths based on one field's value.
chapters.hook: What should happen to the one email out of 30 that says 'urgent'? Nothing, unless you say so.

chapters.title: When a station jams
chapters.covers: The Executions list shows every run, with the failing node marked in red. You read error messages, re-run with the same data, and set a workflow to retry or alert you on failure.
chapters.outcome: You can find which node failed, read why, and fix it without rebuilding the workflow.
chapters.hook: One template line can write 100 personalised messages. Here is the 12-character trick behind it.

chapters.title: Switching the line on for real
chapters.covers: The Active toggle makes a workflow run without you. You pick one real repetitive task from your job, build it end to end, name every node clearly, and check it the next morning.
chapters.outcome: You can turn on one workflow that handles a real task at your job and know where to check that it ran.
chapters.hook: Most workflows fail silently in week 2. One extra node means you hear about it first.

hooksFrom.outcome7: By day 7 you'll be able to build, test and switch on one real workflow for your job: a trigger (a form, a schedule or a new email) that reads data, filters it with an IF step, and posts a formatted message to Slack or a spreadsheet, with an error alert if it fails.
hooksFrom.horizon14: Later: three workflows running unattended, one pulling from a service that has no ready-made n8n block, using a plain web request.
hooksFrom.horizon28: Later: a small 'automation menu' for your team, each workflow documented and owned, replacing 2 to 3 hours of weekly copy-paste.

picture.name: a conveyor belt
picture.line: An n8n workflow is a factory conveyor belt: something drops on at the start, each station does one job to it, and the finished item rolls off the end.

chapters.title: What a workflow actually is
chapters.covers: Trigger, nodes and the data that flows between them; building a 3-node belt that runs when you press a button.
chapters.outcome: You can build and run a 3-node workflow from a blank canvas and read what each node received and sent.
chapters.hook: Every automation you have ever used is three parts. You will build all three in 10 minutes.

chapters.title: Triggers: what starts the belt
chapters.covers: The 4 trigger types you'll use most (manual, schedule, form, webhook) and how to pick one for a real task.
chapters.outcome: You can choose the right trigger for a task and set a schedule that fires at 8am on weekdays.
chapters.hook: A workflow that never starts does nothing. Which of 4 starters does your task need?

chapters.title: Reading the data at each station
chapters.covers: The items-and-fields view, how to spot field names, and why one run can carry 50 items at once.
chapters.outcome: You can open any node's output, name the field you want, and drag it into the next node.
chapters.hook: The box labelled 'name' and the box labelled 'Name' are different. This chapter stops that bug.

chapters.title: Connecting your real tools
chapters.covers: Credentials (saved logins n8n keeps for you), connecting Gmail or Google Sheets and Slack, and a safe test send.
chapters.outcome: You can connect two tools you use at work and move one row of data from one to the other.
chapters.hook: n8n has over 400 ready-made connections. Yours take about 4 minutes each to set up.

chapters.title: Making decisions mid-belt
chapters.covers: The IF and Filter nodes, comparing fields, and sending different items down different paths.
chapters.outcome: You can route urgent items one way and the rest another way, based on a field's value.
chapters.hook: What should happen to the one email out of 30 that says 'urgent'? Nothing, unless you say so.

chapters.title: Shaping the output
chapters.covers: The Edit Fields (Set) node and expressions: small bits of text in double curly braces that pull data into messages.
chapters.outcome: You can write one message that fills itself in with the sender, date and subject from the incoming data.
chapters.hook: One template line can write 100 personalised messages. Here is the 12-character trick behind it.

chapters.title: Switching it on and keeping it alive
chapters.covers: Activating a workflow, reading the executions log, an error workflow that alerts you, and what to check when a run fails.
chapters.outcome: You can activate a workflow, find why a run failed, and get a message when something breaks.
chapters.hook: Most workflows fail silently in week 2. One extra node means you hear about it first.
